passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Now you, son of man, take up a lament for Tyre.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a message.
He called me “son of man.”
He told me to speak about Tyre.
He told me to sing a lament for Tyre.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֔ם שָׂ֥א עַל־ צֹ֖ר קִינָֽה׃

passages.text: Tell Tyre, who dwells at the gateway to the sea, merchant of the peoples on many coasts, that this is what the Lord GOD says: You have said, O Tyre, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’
passages.sermon:
Tyre is a city.
Tyre sits at the gateway to the sea.
Tyre is a merchant for many peoples.
Tyre trades with many coasts and islands.
The Lord GOD speaks to Tyre.
The Lord GOD says this to Tyre.
Tyre, you have said, “I am perfect in beauty.”
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לְצ֗וֹר הַיֹּשַׁבְתִּי עַל־ מְבוֹאֹ֣ת יָ֔ם רֹכֶ֙לֶת֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֶל־ אִיִּ֖ים רַבִּ֑ים כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה צ֕וֹר אַ֣תְּ אָמַ֔רְתְּ אֲנִ֖י כְּלִ֥ילַת יֹֽפִי׃

passages.text: Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders perfected your beauty.
passages.sermon: Tyre is a city.\r\nTyre’s borders are in the heart of the seas.\r\nTyre’s builders perfected Tyre’s beauty.
passages.original: בְּלֵ֥ב יַמִּ֖ים גְּבוּלָ֑יִךְ בֹּנַ֕יִךְ כָּלְל֖וּ יָפְיֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: They constructed all your planking with cypress from Senir. They took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
passages.sermon: The people built all your planks with cypress wood from Senir.\r\nThey took cedar wood from Lebanon.\r\nThey made a mast for you from this cedar.
passages.original: בְּרוֹשִׁ֤ים מִשְּׂנִיר֙ בָּ֣נוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־ לֻֽחֹתָ֑יִם אֶ֤רֶז מִלְּבָנוֹן֙ לָקָ֔חוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת תֹּ֖רֶן עָלָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; of wood from the coasts of Cyprus they made your deck, inlaid with ivory.
passages.sermon: The people used oaks from Bashan to make your oars.\r\nThey used wood from the coasts of Cyprus to make your deck.\r\nThey inlaid your deck with ivory.
passages.original: אַלּוֹנִים֙ מִבָּ֔שָׁן עָשׂ֖וּ מִשּׁוֹטָ֑יִךְ קַרְשֵׁ֤ךְ עָֽשׂוּ־ שֵׁן֙ בַּת־ אֲשֻׁרִ֔ים מֵאִיֵּ֖י כִּתִּיִּם׃

passages.text: Of embroidered fine linen from Egypt they made your sail, which served as your banner. Of blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah they made your awning.
passages.sermon:
Tyre was a great trading city.
People made your sail from fine linen embroidered in Egypt.
This sail became your banner.
People made your awning from blue and purple cloth.
They brought this cloth from the coasts of Elishah.
passages.original: שֵׁשׁ־ בְּרִקְמָ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה מִפְרָשֵׂ֔ךְ לִהְי֥וֹת לָ֖ךְ לְנֵ֑ס תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן מֵאִיֵּ֥י אֱלִישָׁ֖ה הָיָ֥ה מְכַסֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: The men of Sidon and Arvad were your oarsmen. Your men of skill, O Tyre, were there as your captains.
passages.sermon:
The men of Sidon rowed your ships.
The men of Arvad rowed your ships.
Tyre had skilled men.
These skilled men served as your captains.
passages.original: יֹשְׁבֵ֤י צִידוֹן֙ וְאַרְוַ֔ד הָי֥וּ שָׁטִ֖ים לָ֑ךְ חֲכָמַ֤יִךְ צוֹר֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ הֵ֖מָּה חֹבְלָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: The elders of Gebal were aboard as shipwrights, repairing your leaks. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came alongside to barter for your merchandise.
passages.sermon:
The elders of Gebal were with you.
The wise men of Gebal were with you.
They served as your shipwrights.
They repaired your leaks.
All the ships of the sea came to you.
All their sailors came to you.
They came to barter for your merchandise.
passages.original: זִקְנֵ֨י גְבַ֤ל וַחֲכָמֶ֙יהָ֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ מַחֲזִיקֵ֖י בִּדְקֵ֑ךְ כָּל־ אֳנִיּ֨וֹת הַיָּ֤ם וּמַלָּֽחֵיהֶם֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ לַעֲרֹ֖ב מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Men of Persia, Lydia, and Put served as warriors in your army. They hung their shields and helmets on your walls; they gave you splendor.
passages.sermon:
Men from Persia, Lydia, and Put served in your army.
They were your warriors.
They hung their shields on your walls.
They hung their helmets on your walls.
They gave you splendor.
passages.original: פָּרַ֨ס וְל֤וּד וּפוּט֙ הָי֣וּ בְחֵילֵ֔ךְ אַנְשֵׁ֖י מִלְחַמְתֵּ֑ךְ מָגֵ֤ן וְכוֹבַע֙ תִּלּוּ־ בָ֔ךְ הֵ֖מָּה נָתְנ֥וּ הֲדָרֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Men of Arvad and Helech manned your walls all around, and the men of Gammad were in your towers. They hung their shields around your walls; they perfected your beauty.
passages.sermon:
Men from Arvad served as your soldiers.
They guarded your walls on every side.
Men from Helech also served as your soldiers.
They stood on your walls all around.
Men from Gammad stayed in your towers.
They hung their shields on your walls everywhere.
These men made your city beautiful and complete.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֧י אַרְוַ֣ד וְחֵילֵ֗ךְ עַל־ חוֹמוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ סָבִ֔יב וְגַ֨מָּדִ֔ים בְּמִגְדְּלוֹתַ֖יִךְ הָי֑וּ שִׁלְטֵיהֶ֞ם תִּלּ֤וּ עַל־ חוֹמוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ סָבִ֔יב הֵ֖מָּה כָּלְל֥וּ יָפְיֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Tarshish was your merchant because of your great wealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares.
passages.sermon:
Tarshish was a merchant for you.
You had great wealth and many goods.
Tarshish traded with you because of this wealth.
They gave you silver.
They gave you iron.
They gave you tin.
They gave you lead.
They exchanged these for your wares.
passages.original: תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ סֹחַרְתֵּ֖ךְ מֵרֹ֣ב כָּל־ ה֑וֹן בְּכֶ֤סֶף בַּרְזֶל֙ בְּדִ֣יל וְעוֹפֶ֔רֶת נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants. They exchanged slaves and bronze utensils for your merchandise.
passages.sermon:
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were merchants.
They traded with you.
They gave you slaves.
They gave you bronze utensils.
They received your merchandise in return.
passages.original: יָוָ֤ן תֻּבַל֙ וָמֶ֔שֶׁךְ הֵ֖מָּה רֹֽכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ אָדָם֙ וּכְלֵ֣י נְחֹ֔שֶׁת נָתְנ֖וּ מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: The men of Beth-togarmah exchanged horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
passages.sermon:
The men of Beth-togarmah traded with you.
They gave you horses.
They gave you war horses.
They gave you mules.
They gave you these animals in exchange for your goods.
passages.original: מִבֵּ֖ית תּוֹגַרְמָ֑ה סוּסִ֤ים וּפָֽרָשִׁים֙ וּפְרָדִ֔ים נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: The men of Dedan were your clients; many coastlands were your market; they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
passages.sermon:
The men of Dedan traded with you.
Many coastlands bought your goods.
They gave you ivory tusks.
They gave you ebony.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֤י דְדָן֙ רֹֽכְלַ֔יִךְ אִיִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים סְחֹרַ֣ת יָדֵ֑ךְ קַרְנ֥וֹת שֵׁן֙ וְהוֹבְנִים הֵשִׁ֖יבוּ אֶשְׁכָּרֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Aram was your customer because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your wares.
passages.sermon:
Aram was your customer.
Aram traded with you because you had many products.
Aram gave you turquoise.
Aram gave you purple cloth.
Aram gave you embroidered work.
Aram gave you fine linen.
Aram gave you coral.
Aram gave you rubies.
Aram exchanged all these for your wares.
passages.original: אֲרָ֥ם סֹחַרְתֵּ֖ךְ מֵרֹ֣ב מַעֲשָׂ֑יִךְ בְּ֠נֹפֶךְ אַרְגָּמָ֨ן וְרִקְמָ֤ה וּבוּץ֙ וְרָאמֹ֣ת וְכַדְכֹּ֔ד נָתְנ֖וּ בְּעִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, cakes and honey, oil and balm for your merchandise.
passages.sermon:
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you.
They gave you wheat from Minnith.
They gave you cakes.
They gave you honey.
They gave you oil.
They gave you balm.
They gave you these things in exchange for your merchandise.
passages.original: יְהוּדָה֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֵ֖מָּה רֹכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּחִטֵּ֣י מִ֠נִּית וּפַנַּ֨ג וּדְבַ֤שׁ וָשֶׁ֙מֶן֙ וָצֹ֔רִי נָתְנ֖וּ מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Because of your many products and your great wealth of goods, Damascus traded with you wine from Helbon, wool from Zahar, and casks of wine from Izal for your wares. Wrought iron, cassia, and sweet cane were exchanged for your merchandise.
passages.sermon:
Damascus traded with you.
You had many products.
You had great wealth.
Damascus gave you wine from Helbon.
Damascus gave you wool from Zahar.
Damascus gave you casks of wine from Izal.
They gave these things for your wares.
Dan and Javan from Uzal also traded with you.
They gave you wrought iron.
They gave you cassia.
They gave you sweet cane.
They exchanged these for your merchandise.
passages.original: דַּמֶּ֧שֶׂק סֹחַרְתֵּ֛ךְ בְּרֹ֥ב מַעֲשַׂ֖יִךְ מֵרֹ֣ב כָּל־ ה֑וֹן בְּיֵ֥ין חֶלְבּ֖וֹן וְצֶ֥מֶר צָֽחַר׃ וְדָ֤ן וְיָוָן֙ מְאוּזָּ֔ל בְּעִזְבוֹנַ֖יִךְ נָתָ֑נּוּ בַּרְזֶ֤ל עָשׁוֹת֙ קִדָּ֣ה וְקָנֶ֔ה בְּמַעֲרָבֵ֖ךְ הָיָֽה׃

passages.text: Dedan was your merchant in saddlecloths for riding.
passages.sermon:
Dedan was a merchant.
Dedan traded with you.
Dedan gave you saddlecloths.
These saddlecloths were for riding.
passages.original: דְּדָן֙ רֹֽכַלְתֵּ֔ךְ בְבִגְדֵי־ חֹ֖פֶשׁ לְרִכְבָּֽה׃

passages.text: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers, trading in lambs, rams, and goats.
passages.sermon:
Arabia traded with you.
All the princes of Kedar traded with you.
They were your customers.
They gave you lambs.
They gave you rams.
They gave you goats.
Your merchants received these animals from them.
passages.original: עֲרַב֙ וְכָל־ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י קֵדָ֔ר הֵ֖מָּה סֹחֲרֵ֣י יָדֵ֑ךְ בְּכָרִ֤ים וְאֵילִים֙ וְעַתּוּדִ֔ים בָּ֖ם סֹחֲרָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; for your wares they exchanged gold, the finest of all spices, and precious stones.
passages.sermon:
The merchants of Sheba traded with you.
The merchants of Raamah traded with you.
They gave you gold for your goods.
They gave you the finest spices for your goods.
They gave you precious stones for your goods.
passages.original: רֹכְלֵ֤י שְׁבָא֙ וְרַעְמָ֔ה הֵ֖מָּה רֹכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּרֹ֨אשׁ כָּל־ בֹּ֜שֶׂם וּבְכָל־ אֶ֤בֶן יְקָרָה֙ וְזָהָ֔ב נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Haran, Canneh, and Eden traded with you, and so did the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad.
passages.sermon:
Haran traded with you.
Canneh traded with you.
Eden traded with you.
The merchants of Sheba traded with you.
Asshur traded with you.
Chilmad traded with you.
passages.original: חָרָ֤ן וְכַנֵּה֙ וָעֶ֔דֶן רֹכְלֵ֖י שְׁבָ֑א אַשּׁ֖וּר כִּלְמַ֥ד רֹכַלְתֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: In your marketplace they traded with you fine garments of blue, embroidered work, and multicolored rugs with cords tightly twisted and knotted.
passages.sermon:
The merchants traded with you in your marketplace.
They brought fine garments of blue.
They brought embroidered work.
They brought multicolored rugs.
These rugs had cords that were tightly twisted and knotted.
They offered all these goods as part of your trade.
passages.original: הֵ֤מָּה רֹכְלַ֙יִךְ֙ בְּמַכְלֻלִ֔ים בִּגְלוֹמֵי֙ תְּכֵ֣לֶת וְרִקְמָ֔ה וּבְגִנְזֵ֖י בְּרֹמִ֑ים בַּחֲבָלִ֧ים חֲבֻשִׁ֛ים וַאֲרֻזִ֖ים בְּמַרְכֻלְתֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: The ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise. And you were filled with heavy cargo in the heart of the sea.
passages.sermon: The ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise.\r\nYou were filled with heavy cargo.\r\nThis happened in the heart of the sea.
passages.original: אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֔ישׁ שָׁרוֹתַ֖יִךְ מַעֲרָבֵ֑ךְ וַתִּמָּלְאִ֧י וַֽתִּכְבְּדִ֛י מְאֹ֖ד בְּלֵ֥ב־ יַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: Your oarsmen have brought you onto the high seas, but the east wind will shatter you in the heart of the sea.
passages.sermon: Your oarsmen brought you onto the high seas.\r\nThe east wind will shatter you in the heart of the sea.
passages.original: בְּמַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ הֱבִיא֔וּךְ הַשָּׁטִ֖ים אֹתָ֑ךְ ר֚וּחַ הַקָּדִ֔ים שְׁבָרֵ֖ךְ בְּלֵ֥ב יַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: Your wealth, wares, and merchandise, your sailors, captains, and shipwrights, your merchants and all the warriors within you, with all the other people on board, will sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your downfall.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes the city of Tyre.
Tyre was a wealthy trading city.
Tyre had much wealth.
Tyre had many goods and merchandise.
Tyre had sailors.
Tyre had captains.
Tyre had shipwrights.
Tyre had merchants.
Tyre had warriors inside her.
Tyre had many other people among her.
All these people and all this wealth will sink.
They will sink into the heart of the sea.
This will happen on the day of Tyre’s downfall.
passages.original: הוֹנֵךְ֙ וְעִזְבוֹנַ֔יִךְ מַעֲרָבֵ֕ךְ מַלָּחַ֖יִךְ וְחֹבְלָ֑יִךְ מַחֲזִיקֵ֣י בִדְקֵ֣ך וְֽעֹרְבֵ֣י מַ֠עֲרָבֵךְ וְכָל־ אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתֵּ֜ךְ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֗ךְ וּבְכָל־ קְהָלֵךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹכֵ֔ךְ יִפְּלוּ֙ בְּלֵ֣ב יַמִּ֔ים בְּי֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: The countryside will shake when your sailors cry out.
passages.sermon:
The sailors are on the ship.
The sailors cry out loudly.
The countryside hears the sailors’ cries.
The countryside shakes because of the sailors’ cries.
passages.original: לְק֖וֹל זַעֲקַ֣ת חֹבְלָ֑יִךְ יִרְעֲשׁ֖וּ מִגְרֹשֽׁוֹת׃

passages.text: All who handle the oars will abandon their ships. The sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore.
passages.sermon:
Tyre was a great city by the sea.
Tyre had many ships.
Many men worked on these ships.
Some men rowed with oars.
Some men were sailors.
Some men were captains.
All these men will leave their ships.
They will go down from their ships.
They will stand on the land.
passages.original: וְֽיָרְד֞וּ מֵאָנִיּֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּ֚ל תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָשׁ֔וֹט מַלָּחִ֕ים כֹּ֖ל חֹבְלֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם אֶל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ יַעֲמֹֽדוּ׃

passages.text: They will raise their voices for you and cry out bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
passages.sermon:
The sailors and captains of the sea will mourn for you, Tyre.
They will raise their voices for you.
They will cry out with bitter sorrow.
They will throw dust on their heads.
They will roll in ashes.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁמִ֤יעוּ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ בְּקוֹלָ֔ם וְיִזְעֲק֖וּ מָרָ֑ה וְיַעֲל֤וּ עָֽפָר֙ עַל־ רָ֣אשֵׁיהֶ֔ם בָּאֵ֖פֶר יִתְפַּלָּֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: They will shave their heads for you and wrap themselves in sackcloth. They will weep over you with anguish of soul and bitter mourning.
passages.sermon:
The people will mourn for you, Tyre.
They will shave their heads.
They will put on sackcloth.
They will weep for you.
They will feel deep anguish in their souls.
They will mourn for you with bitter sorrow.
passages.original: וְהִקְרִ֤יחוּ אֵלַ֙יִךְ֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְחָגְר֖וּ שַׂקִּ֑ים וּבָכ֥וּ אֵלַ֛יִךְ בְּמַר־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ מִסְפֵּ֥ד מָֽר׃

passages.text: As they wail and mourn over you, they will take up a lament for you: ‘Who was ever like Tyre, silenced in the middle of the sea?
passages.sermon:
The people mourn for you, Tyre.
They wail and cry out for you.
They sing a song of sorrow about you.
They say, “Who is like Tyre?”
No one is like Tyre in the middle of the sea.
Tyre is now silent and destroyed.
passages.original: וְנָשְׂא֨וּ אֵלַ֤יִךְ בְּנִיהֶם֙ קִינָ֔ה וְקוֹנְנ֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ מִ֣י כְצ֔וֹר כְּדֻמָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: When your wares went out to sea, you satisfied many nations. You enriched the kings of the earth with your abundant wealth and merchandise.
passages.sermon:
Tyre was a powerful and wealthy city.
Tyre sent its goods and merchandise out to sea.
Many nations received these goods from Tyre.
These nations became satisfied because of Tyre’s trade.
Tyre had great wealth and many valuable products.
Tyre’s wealth and merchandise made the kings of the earth rich.
passages.original: בְּצֵ֤את עִזְבוֹנַ֙יִךְ֙ מִיַּמִּ֔ים הִשְׂבַּ֖עַתְּ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים בְּרֹ֤ב הוֹנַ֙יִךְ֙ וּמַ֣עֲרָבַ֔יִךְ הֶעֱשַׁ֖רְתְּ מַלְכֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Now you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and the people among you have gone down with you.
passages.sermon:
Tyre was a powerful city.
Tyre traded goods across the seas.
Now the seas have broken Tyre.
The city is shattered in the deep waters.
All your merchandise has fallen with you.
All your people inside you have fallen too.
passages.original: עֵ֛ת נִשְׁבֶּ֥רֶת מִיַּמִּ֖ים בְּמַֽעֲמַקֵּי־ מָ֑יִם מַעֲרָבֵ֥ךְ וְכָל־ קְהָלֵ֖ךְ בְּתוֹכֵ֥ךְ נָפָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: All the people of the coastlands are appalled over you. Their kings shudder with fear; their faces are contorted.
passages.sermon:
The people who live on the coastlands see you.
They are shocked because of you.
Their kings are afraid.
Their kings tremble.
Their faces show fear.
passages.original: כֹּ֚ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאִיִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ וּמַלְכֵיהֶם֙ שָׂ֣עֲרוּ שַׂ֔עַר רָעֲמ֖וּ פָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: Those who trade among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end and will be no more.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Traders from many nations see you.
They hiss at you.
You have reached a terrible end.
You will never exist again.
passages.original: סֹֽחֲרִים֙ בָּ֣עַמִּ֔ים שָׁרְק֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃ס
